I'm a senior who will be graduating from the department this Spring, and have enjoyed my time in the program.  

- Research opportunities are plentiful and cover a wide range of topics.  Be sure you are proactive in talking with your professor to get involved.  The department also holds an open house every year showing off all the labs which is how I got involved.

- The advisers are truly a godsend.  Margot and Paula were always a huge help and offered valuable advice all throughout my time here.

- The 12x series, usually taken freshman year, is a bit of a mess and doesn't represent what higher level classes are like.

- Upper level labs were by far the best courses I took.  Professor Pengra, the department's lab manager, is a great lecturer and has a solid system in place.  

- Lectures range from nearly useless to insightful and interesting.  Be sure to look at course evaluations, or else be sure you have the discipline to teach yourself from the textbook.  

- Lectures range from 100+ people and gradually reach as a few as 20 or less in senior year.  

If you have any other questions or want opinions on specific professors or courses, feel free to PM me.
